# 1. Snapshot the three catalog files at FULL precision. Use $env:USERPROFILE, never a typed path with non-ASCII characters (phase A lost a whole run to ANSI/GBK decoding of a Chinese path, boundary-audit.md:57). Never open or hash catalog.sqlite3.
# 2. Hash ONLY the side files, and tolerate refusal - refusal is itself a datum (it means a foreign process holds the catalog open right now).

foreach ($f in 'catalog.sqlite3-wal','catalog.sqlite3-shm') { try { (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath (Join-Path $c $f) -Algorithm SHA256 -ErrorAction Stop).Hash } catch { "BLOCKED $f : $($_.Exception.Message)" } }
# 3. List the whole .source_catalog tree by mtime so scheduled writers are visible, not just the three catalog files.
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $c -Force | Sort-Object LastWriteTime | Select-Object Name,Length,LastWriteTime | Format-Table -AutoSize

# 4. THE KEY STEP - establish the machine's own baseline motion BEFORE the session. Poll every 2 s for 120 s doing nothing else, and count transitions. If the baseline is non-zero, a later move proves nothing about the session.
# 5. Anchor every repository tree. Record that these are point-in-time, and re-run them at the end.

foreach ($r in 'company-wiki','revenue-forecast','filing-fetch') { $p = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "Projects\$r"; "== $r =="; git -C $p rev-parse HEAD; git -C $p rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD; git -C $p status --porcelain; git -C $p log -1 --format='%H|%cI|%s' }
# 6. Anchor the run directory itself so the audit trail's own motion is visible.
# 7. Write the whole output of steps 0-6 to ONE file OUTSIDE the three repositories (a before-snapshot is worthless inside a tree the session may commit).
after: # Re-run steps 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 of 'before' VERBATIM and diff the two files. Do not paraphrase or re-type the commands; a changed command is a different measurement.
# Then re-run the baseline poll of step 4 so the after-window's own noise is measured too, then compare like with like:
# Verdict rules, in order of strength:
# (A) catalog.sqlite3 Length or LastWriteTime changed  => a persisted write is very likely; this is the strongest available positive signal and needs no attribution to be alarming.
# (B) catalog.sqlite3-wal Length > 0  => uncommitted/uncheckpointed frames exist; treat as a write.
# (C) -shm advanced while the baseline poll (step 4) was flat AND no scheduled task, push or test run is known  => a new open occurred; the session is a candidate but NOT identified.
# (D) -shm advanced but the baseline poll also advanced  => NO conclusion about the session. This is the case on this host today.
# (E) Get-FileHash on -wal/-shm refused with 'being used by another process'  => a process holds the catalog open at that instant; it proves an open, never a write, and names no one.
detects: Whether the production database FILE changed: catalog.sqlite3 Length and LastWriteTime. This is the one signal that is currently clean, because it did not budge across my whole window while -shm moved four times.
Whether uncommitted write frames exist: catalog.sqlite3-wal Length (0 or not).

Whether SOME process opened the catalog at some point between the two snapshots: -shm LastWriteTime advancing beyond the before-value - valid ONLY if the step-4 baseline was flat and the known openers were idle.

Whether a process holds the catalog open RIGHT NOW: a 'being used by another process' refusal when reading -wal/-shm. This is a real, currently-reproducible instrument: it fired for me at ~22:58 and it did not fire at ~22:55, so it is intermittent and its positive result is meaningful.
Scheduled and out-of-session writers, via the whole-directory mtime listing: this is how I found legacy_periods.json written at 2026-09-15 22:00:41 with no session involved.

Which files a session touched in the tracked trees: git status --porcelain plus the run-directory mtime listing. This is the only part of the protocol that reliably attributes anything, and it attributes WORKING-TREE files, not database opens.
Whether the tree moved at all during the window: re-running rev-parse HEAD at the end caught a concurrent commit (89494e07 -> 81817c47) that no mtime reading would have surfaced as cleanly.
cannot_detect: A past open. NTFS holds one mtime; -shm is overwritten every time. The authoring window (2026-09-12..2026-09-13) is closed and NOTHING in this protocol can reach back into it. This is the central limitation of gate G5 and no amount of future care removes it.

A read-only open that writes nothing and takes no conflicting share mode. If it coincides with the machine's own baseline accessor - which on this host touches the catalog roughly every 10-90 seconds - it leaves no distinguishable trace at all.
A logical write that was rolled back, or one that was checkpointed and then had its timestamps restored: the observed value would be identical to no-write.

WHICH process caused any given -shm advance. Attribution needs handle enumeration (Sysinternals handle.exe), ETW/Procmon, or an object-access audit policy with a SACL on the database file; phase A already recorded all three as unavailable on this Windows 11 home machine without administrator tooling (boundary-audit.md:94-98), and installing them is itself an environment change that needs owner authorization. I confirmed the practical consequence: after 18 distinct sets of transient python.exe PIDs in 45 seconds, I could not name the opener.

Whether a CLI of the product was executed. There is no process-launch log, no shell history I am permitted to consult as evidence, and running the CLI to test the question is forbidden. 'No CLI was executed' is therefore permanently a declaration, not a measurement - it can only ever be corroborated by its absence from other artefacts.

Whether an open was READ-ONLY. -shm movement is identical for read-only and read-write opens (the mechanism the run itself states at boundary-audit.md:21). Only the main DB / -wal changing separates them, and only for writes that actually persisted.

LastAccessTime as evidence. It is updated by the observer's own reads (mine moved to 22:55:07 on a Get-FileHash) and is then overwritten by the next writer; it is also subject to lazy/disabled last-access updates. Treat it as noise.

Anything about a session that runs while another session is active. Two concurrent actors produce one interleaved mtime stream; my own window is the worked example - I could not separate the concurrent session's catalog opens from any other cause.
protocol.conclusion_for_g5: On this host, at this time, the -shm instrument is SATURATED and therefore cannot support any claim in either direction about a specific session. The only currently-clean signals are (i) catalog.sqlite3 Length/LastWriteTime, which supports 'no persisted write since 2026-09-08' and (ii) the -wal Length, which supports 'no uncheckpointed frames'. Both are consistent with the authoring session's no-write claim and neither can attribute it. The 'no CLI executed' half of the claim is not merely unverified - it is structurally unverifiable by read-only observation and should be re-worded in the run's ledger as a declaration rather than carried forward as a boundary result.

not_done: Did NOT run any CLI of the wiki product - not even --help - and did not run pytest or invoke any project python module.
Did NOT open, query, copy, read the bytes of, or hash catalog.sqlite3. Its content is untouched by me; only Length, LastWriteTime, CreationTime, LastAccessTime and Attributes were read via Get-Item.

Did NOT run any network command: no web request, no git fetch/pull/push/ls-remote, no download, no package install. Consequently the CI run ids and 'the run directory IS pushed' sub-claim were NOT re-verified against GitHub.
Did NOT write anything except this record file. No other file was created, edited, moved, renamed or deleted; no git add/commit/checkout/reset/stash/clean/push in any of the three repositories.
Did NOT touch .tmp-zr408-unit, .tmp-zr408-unit-final or .tmp-zr408-unit-retry, nor the .review-zr407-* permission-denied artefacts; they are visible only as the three stderr warnings in git status.
Did NOT request or attempt any sandbox escalation; no command was denied by the sandbox during this observation.
Did NOT attempt handle-level, ETW, Procmon or audit-policy forensics, and did NOT install any tool.
Did NOT verify the historical -shm values and make no claim about them beyond 'not observable'.
Did NOT identify the concurrent session or the process that holds the catalog open; I only established that both exist.

Did NOT read the phase-A reviews/A.DR.json, phase-a/checkpoint.json, baseline/a06-d0-baseline.md or the run's evidence/*.json in full; where a record was needed I read the sections the task named (checkpoint.json, findings.md G5/disposition rows, progress.md boundary tables, owner-scope-decisions-2026-09-13.md, phase-a/boundary-audit.md).
notes: WHAT THIS OBSERVATION ACTUALLY SETTLES. The short answer is: it confirms the boundary state that is still observable, and it demonstrates that the historical claim is now formally UNFALSIFIABLE rather than merely unverified. Three findings carry the weight. (1) A CONCURRENT SESSION was active during my observation, in the same run directory: revenue-forecast HEAD moved from 89494e0720ab881191f8142c1093ece3a7e52ad9 (commit 'docs(r4b0x): CI rows for the three-repo gate rollout (all green)', 2026-09-15T22:26:49+01:00) to 81817c470b5055463b2520fe1433c3aeb6230df5 ('feat(zr902): the daily T2 loop gets the same blocked/not-ok split (owner decision)', 2026-09-15T22:57:16+01:00) between 22:55 and 22:58:34 local; the previously-untracked owner-scope-decisions-2026-09-13.md was committed in that interval; and a new file evidence/zr902_mutations.py was created at 22:56:31 and written at 22:56:55. So no repo anchor I record is a frozen tree, and any future observer must re-anchor rather than quote mine. (2) The -shm instrument is a MOVING TARGET with a high idle rate: it advanced at least four times inside a 2.5-minute window (22:55:32, 22:56:02.5, 22:56:12.8, 22:57:41.3 local) while I did nothing but stat it, while catalog.sqlite3 stayed frozen at 2026-09-08T22:23:21.0727473+01:00 and -wal stayed 0 bytes at 2026-09-13T00:01:27.9844681+01:00. Both passive windows (60 s and 45 s, stat-only) recorded transitions, which is the cleanest proof that the movement is external to the observer. At ~22:58 the OS then refused to let me read -wal and -shm at all ('being used by another process'), which is direct evidence of a foreign open at that instant. Phase A's calibration (boundary-audit.md:21/:66) therefore reproduces, but its USE as an attribution instrument does not: with a ~10-90 s ambient cadence, a single before/after -shm comparison carries essentially zero information about one session. (3) The one clean, genuinely checkable fact that favours the run's no-write claim: catalog.sqlite3 has not been written since 2026-09-08T22:23:21+01:00, which PREDATES the authoring window (2026-09-12..2026-09-13) by four days, and it is still that value on 2026-09-15 - and -wal is 0 bytes. So there is currently no observable evidence of a persisted logical write during the window. That is the strongest support the run gets from me, and it is support for 'no persisted write', not for 'the catalog was never opened' and not for 'no CLI ran'. THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART, recorded because it is the point of an independent observation: the run's own phase-A record at boundary-audit.md:15 asserted that `-wal` was frozen at 2026-09-08 22:23:21 with 0 bytes; the length still holds but the mtime is now 2026-09-13T00:01:27.9844681+01:00, inside the authoring window, and the file object was not recreated (CreationTime still 2026-09-04T09:07:46). I do NOT read that as evidence of a write - a read-only open can reset the WAL header, and checkpoint.json:230 discloses that full pytest runs during the window opened the production catalog - but it does mean the corresponding sentences must stop being quoted as present-tense facts, and it is the kind of drift that a single-snapshot boundary claim cannot survive. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE G5. Not this file. The honest closing condition is a change of claim: strike 'no CLI was executed, no production data was touched' from the run's results and re-register it, as findings.md:457 already does, as a DECLARATION that no read-only instrument on this host can confirm or refute - and then, for any FUTURE session, run the before/after protocol above on a quiet machine so that the bracket is meaningful. If the owner wants attribution rather than detection, the only real remedies are environment changes outside my authority: a SACL plus auditpol object-access auditing on catalog.sqlite3, or Procmon/ETW capture during the session. Finally, a caution about my own evidence: the machine was demonstrably busy with another agent while I worked, so even the 'clean' main-DB signal is a statement about 2026-09-15T21:54Z..21:58Z only, and it should be re-measured before anyone relies on it.
